newsitem.title: UK: INSTANT VIEW - UK November RPI data.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW - UK November RPI data.

text.p: Following is a selection of economists' reactions to UK data showing November RPI up 0.1 percent m/m and 2.7 percent y/y, with RPIX up 0.1 percent m/m and 3.3 percent y/y:

"A very dull set of numbers. I don't think we're going to see much reaction from gilts or sterling. They are in some ways disappointing because obviously inflation needs to be falling and it's looking fairly stagnant."

"The fact that inflation is stable means that people have to have doubts whether we're going to hit the inflation target in the middle of next year and you have to have doubts about the Chancellor's argument that it was just a blip. Clearly, inflation is staying high and above the expectations of the authorities. I think it means pressures are going to build for higher rates."

"As in October, inflation looks good on a month on month basis but less good on a year on year basis, since trend price rises a year ago were smaller than at present. Strengthening domestic demand, an ever tightening labour market and strong monetary growth suggest inflation will not fall back to the government's target zone. Interesting that clothing and footwear prices rose 1.1 percent in November. This has been one of the strongest areas of retail spending and certainly points to margin-building in that area."

"It's basically in line with the market forecast. Numbers on the household goods end a bit worrying as that could boost retail prices later on. But of course in the short-term we'll see sterling strength feeding through, benefiting foods. Retailers have been trying to increase their margins and going forward, interest rates may have to go up to dampen retail strength."
